Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.24. Source: Kubernetes v1.24.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.24.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Kubeadm: graduated the UnversionedKubeletConfigMap feature gate to Beta and enabled the feature by default. This implies that 1) for new clusters kubeadm will start using the kube-system/kubelet-config naming scheme for the kubelet ConfigMap and RBAC rules, instead of the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy naming. 2) during upgrade, kubeadm will only write the new scheme ConfigMap and RBAC objects. To disable the feature you can pass UnversionedKubeletConfigMap: false in the kubeadm config for new clusters. For upgrade on existing clusters you can also override the behavior by patching the ClusterConfiguration object in kube-system/kubeadm-config. More details in the associated KEP.
>>>

To disable the feature you can pass UnversionedKubeletConfigMap: false in the kubeadm config for new clusters. For upgrade on existing clusters you can also override the behavior by patching the ClusterConfiguration object in kube-system/kubeadm-config. More details in the associated KEP. Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.24 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: kubeadm legacy kubelet ConfigMap naming during upgrade
paths.description: Kubeadm now uses the kube-system/kubelet-config naming scheme for the kubelet ConfigMap and RBAC rules, and during upgrade it only writes the new scheme objects instead of the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy naming. The text does not state what breaks for consumers of the legacy objects.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 1.24, where the UnversionedKubeletConfigMap feature gate was graduated to Beta and enabled by default.
quotes: graduated the UnversionedKubeletConfigMap feature gate to Beta and enabled the feature by default
conditions.relevance: Ties the kubelet ConfigMap naming change to the 1.23 to 1.29 upgrade path.

conditions.statement: The cluster is managed by kubeadm and has kubelet ConfigMap or RBAC objects that use the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy naming.
quotes: instead of the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy naming
conditions.relevance: The risk applies only to clusters or tooling that depend on the legacy naming scheme.
ambiguities: The text does not state which consumers or tooling read the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy objects, or what breaks when they are absent.

conditions.statement: The UnversionedKubeletConfigMap feature has been disabled by patching ClusterConfiguration in kube-system/kubeadm-config, which avoids the new-scheme-only behavior on upgrade.
quotes: For upgrade on existing clusters you can also override the behavior by patching the ClusterConfiguration object in kube-system/kubeadm-config
conditions.relevance: If the override is in place, the upgrade does not switch to writing only the new scheme objects.
ambiguities: The text does not state the exact patched value; it only says the behavior can be overridden, while the false setting is stated only for new clusters.

search_queries.query: kubectl get configmap kubeadm-config -n kube-system -o yaml

suggested_actions: Check whether kubelet ConfigMap or RBAC objects for the legacy kubelet-config-x.yy naming exist and whether any tooling reads them.
Before upgrading an existing kubeadm cluster, review the kube-system/kubeadm-config ClusterConfiguration override if you need to keep the legacy behavior.
